precise_scope: Supplied surjective holomorphic pi:X->B between connected smooth compact Kahler manifolds, dim X=n>nu=dim B>=1, beta Kahler, theta=pi*beta, m=n-nu. Critical and dimension-jumping fibres included, with no connected-fibre assumption for the main theorem. Globally bounded beta-psh phi and bounded admissible u_epsilon uniformly converging to pi*phi; u_epsilon need not descend and no epsilon-relative rate is required. All auxiliary Kahler classes after the explicit c_omega=pi_*(omega^m)>0 calibration; smoothly converging auxiliary paths with Kahler limit included. Raw base mass is int_B beta^nu. Unnormalized energy divided by binom(n,nu)c_epsilon epsilon^m converges to E_beta(phi), and corresponding relative energies converge. Exact bounded shift, cocycle, monotonicity, concavity, affine variation and C1 uniform paths in C(B) with continuous velocities are proved. The calibrated base operator is supporting. Base representative changes have an explicit reference cocycle. Optional continuous descent requires connected fibres. This requires a supplied fibration and pullback Kahler class. No canonical carrier for general pseudoeffective classes, minimum necessary reference data, unbounded prescribed singularity type or E1 completion, or arbitrary degenerate auxiliary path is proved. The original problem remains open.

source_status.exact_result: For a supplied surjective holomorphic map pi:X->B between connected smooth compact Kahler manifolds, dim X=n>nu=dim B>=1, beta Kahler and theta=pi*beta, the bounded unnormalized relative base energy E_beta is the limit of E_(theta+epsilon omega_epsilon)(u_epsilon)/(binom(n,nu)c_epsilon epsilon^(n-nu)) for any bounded admissible u_epsilon uniformly converging to pi*phi, with no epsilon-relative rate and no descent assumption. Here c_epsilon=pi_*(omega_epsilon^(n-nu)) is a positive constant; omega_epsilon may converge smoothly to any Kahler form in any class. The limit has raw mass int_B beta^nu and exact bounded shift, cocycle, monotonicity, concavity, affine variational and continuous C1 uniform-path first-variation laws. A supporting calibrated pushforward estimate is proved across singular fibres. Representative changes on the base require the stated reference cocycle. Optional continuous descent holds for connected fibres.
concrete_gaps: The original general pseudoeffective zero-volume P15.1 remains open; the theorem requires a supplied holomorphic fibration with a pullback Kahler class.
No canonical carrier/map or proof of the minimum necessary reference scale for general classes is supplied; changing the carrier pi is not covered.
No prescribed unbounded P-singularity type, E1 completion, or unbounded-potential perturbation theorem is proved.
No arbitrary degenerate auxiliary paths and no variational theorem for arbitrary discontinuous velocities are claimed.
This is an unverified author draft relying on explicitly stated standard bounded BT/IBP and geometric foundations; no independent model verdict or formal proof certificate was produced.

result.report:
The argument establishes the exact bounded, supplied-fibration result, including singular fibres, arbitrary non-descending admissible approximants, uniform convergence without an ε-relative rate, smoothly converging auxiliary Kähler directions, the reference cocycle, and optional continuous descent for connected fibres. It does not establish the explicitly excluded general zero-volume problem.

The external foundations listed below were checked against opened primary bodies. Every integration-by-parts application satisfies the bounded special case with A empty: the functions are bounded quasi-psh functions or differences thereof, and the remaining mixed current is closed, positive, and of bidimension (1,1). No global smooth approximation in the original class, unbounded-product theorem, or boundary removal at critical fibres is needed.

The degree-zero pushforward argument is valid. Proper pushforward preserves closedness, so π*(ω^m) is a constant distribution on connected B. Sard applies to the smooth map of real dimensions 2n and 2ν; surjectivity therefore supplies a full-rank point. Consequently ∫X θ^ν ω^m is positive, establishing formula (5), positivity of c, and its fixed-class representative independence. Closedness excludes any additional critical-value-supported distribution. Ordinary submersion integration verifies the stated regular-fibre interpretation, including disconnected regular fibres.

The bounded projection proof establishes its claimed scope across all fibres. Multiplication by bounded Borel base functions commutes with pushforward of order-zero currents, as follows directly from coefficient measures. Combined with the BT recursion and commutation with dd^c, this proves (6) and the discontinuous-weight identity (7). Local decreasing smooth approximations also show that more than ν pulled-back factors vanish, including at critical points. The global identity dd^c(wS) and Stokes justify every mixed-mass replacement, including semipositive θ. These facts establish numerical dimension ν, zero volume, and the leading perturbative volume KcV_B ε^m.

The energy coefficient calculation is correct: counting subsets by their (a+1)-st element gives the stated Vandermonde identity, and division by n+1 yields K/(ν+1). Weighted projection supplies exactly the base energy. Every remaining coefficient has uniformly bounded mass and an additional ε factor. Smooth convergence of the auxiliary forms ensures these bounds and keeps c_ε away from zero. The bounded energy Lipschitz estimate then gives (16): the approximation error is δ_ε(V_B+O(ε)), rather than an error divided by a power of ε. This establishes (1) without a rate condition; the exact energy-difference identity establishes (2).

The supporting measure estimate also checks out. Factoring the difference of powers and testing against f∘π produces nC_fδ_ε I_ε. Cohomology gives I_ε/s_ε=(ν/n)V_B+O(ε), so the calibrated error tends to zero with δ_ε. The exact pullback expansion has the stated leading measure and a positive remainder of calibrated mass O(ε). Uniform total-mass bounds extend convergence from smooth to continuous tests. Thus (3) holds across critical values. Total-variation convergence is correctly restricted to the exact pullback family.

The bounded energy laws follow with their exact constants. Polynomial differentiation and integration by parts telescope to (9); the beta integral gives the mixed relative formula and cocycle. Positivity gives monotonicity, the shift is bV_B, and the uniform Lipschitz constant is V_B. The gradient-square second variation has the correct negative sign and proves concavity for bounded affine segments. For C1 paths in C(Y), the smooth-test estimate for mixed measures and uniform convergence of difference quotients prove (13); continuity of the derivative follows from the same weak convergence and continuous velocities. No derivative of an arbitrary ε-dependent path is inferred.

The representative-change formulas (21)–(22) are correct, including the positive-ε identity. The dd^c lemma applies to the smooth, real, cohomologically trivial (1,1) difference; its pure type and closedness also give d^c-closedness. Absolute energy changes by the reference correction, while relative energy is invariant under the simultaneous potential transformation.

The optional descent proof is valid. Each reduced irreducible fibre component admits the stated compact resolution; finite continuous psh pullbacks are constant by the maximum principle. Connectedness propagates constants through the finite component intersection graph. The quotient-map argument gives continuity downstairs, and the positive-current pushforward proves β-psh positivity at critical values as well.

No substantial repair is required. The harmless source typographical corrections already flagged in the draft are appropriate: the repeated limit target in Theorem 1.14 should contain u, and the Cauchy–Schwarz current should be Θ. Proposition 2.8's omitted energy prefactor is not used. Lemma 1.5, as supplied, needs eventual exhaustion rather than merely union coverage; it is expressly excluded and supports no indispensable step. Hashes, compilation, prior verdicts, and the operator proposal supply no mathematical evidence for this verdict.

passages.statement: On a complex manifold of dimension d, locally bounded psh functions p1,…,pr, with r≤d, define closed positive Bedford–Taylor products recursively by dd^c(p1S). These products are symmetric, multilinear, and determined by the currents dd^c pi. Mixed products converge weakly when each potential decreases to a locally bounded psh limit. On smaller coordinate domains, locally bounded psh functions admit decreasing smooth psh regularizations. Bedford–Taylor, A new capacity for plurisubharmonic functions (1982), Section 2.

passages.statement: On a compact Kähler manifold Y, let Θ be a closed positive current of bidimension (1,1), and let a1,a2,b1,b2 be globally bounded quasi-psh functions. For a=a1−a2 and b=b1−b2, the bounded products are finite and satisfy ∫Y a dd^c b∧Θ=∫Y b dd^c a∧Θ=−∫Y db∧d^c a∧Θ. The gradient square da∧d^c a∧Θ is a positive finite measure. BEGZ, Theorem 1.14 and Lemma 1.15, with A empty.
passages.quote: ∫_{X−A} u dd^c v∧Θ = ∫_{X−A} v dd^c u∧Θ = −∫_{X−A} dv∧d^c u∧Θ.

passages.statement: For nef real (1,1) classes on a compact Kähler manifold, positive intersection products equal ordinary cup products. Positive products on pseudoeffective classes are defined by limits from Kähler perturbations; the resulting top product gives the nef volume, including boundary classes. BEGZ, Definition 1.17 and subsequent discussion.

For a C^r map from a real a-dimensional smooth manifold to a real b-dimensional smooth manifold, where a>b≥1 and r≥a−b+1, the values attained at points of differential rank less than b have b-dimensional measure zero. Sard, The measure of the critical values of differentiable maps (1942).
